title: To amend title 36, United States Code, to authorize the American Battle Monuments Commission to acquire, operate, and maintain the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial in Marnes-la-Coquette, France, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on September 12, 2016. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

(Sec. 1) This bill authorizes the American Battle Monuments Commission to enter into an agreement with the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial Foundation to acquire, operate, and maintain the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial in Marnes-la-Coquette, France.

The Commission shall ensure the ongoing maintenance of the memorial, including the cemetery containing the remains of 49 U.S. aviators who died during World War I.

summary.headline: This law lets the American Battle Monuments Commission take over, run, and maintain the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial in France.
summary.what_it_does: The law allows the American Battle Monuments Commission to make an agreement with the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial Foundation. Under that agreement, the Commission can acquire, operate, and maintain the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial in Marnes-la-Coquette, France. The Commission must make sure the memorial, including the cemetery there, is kept up over time. The cemetery holds the remains of 49 U.S. aviators who died in World War I.

who_it_affects.how: It gains authority to take on ownership, operation, and upkeep of the memorial and must keep it maintained.
It may enter into an agreement with the Commission to transfer the memorial's acquisition, operation, and maintenance.

who_it_affects.group: Families and descendants of the 49 U.S. aviators buried there
who_it_affects.how: The graves and cemetery are to be kept maintained under federal oversight.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on September 29, 2016; the summary does not list a separate later date.
